title: Into the Shardfall - baked in dev tools for auditing art/balancing
author: Ecstatic-Bend-104
selftext:
Made the mistake of posting this to r/godot and got flamed by the high ‘n’ mighty’s there for using ai lol. 

Anyways, here’s some tools that i had codex create inside my prototype’s project files so i could get the art to a passable state for first distribution, balance encounters, and debug for loops/difficulty level. Figured those who lack artistic talent may find the concepts useful.

I’m no artist, so my goal is to raise funds to get rid of the generated art/animation and replace it with that of an actual artist. If you’re interested in the core gameplay, support my game here! 

[https://bat-mo.itch.io/into-the-shardfall](https://bat-mo.itch.io/into-the-shardfall)

comments.author: Ecstatic-Bend-104
comments.body: Should i add the debug-autorun tool as a togglable feature to the (late) game? I built it to target infinite loops and catch errors but I kind of enjoy watching it play better than I ever could.

comments.author: Epyx911
comments.body: That is my plan as well for my project. Im using AI art currently...tiles were asset from UnityStore but funds for an artist would be great. Good job!

comments.author: AguilaAurea
comments.body: Me gustó mucho tu proyecto. Estoy haciendo un juego táctico también. Puedo preguntarte hacerca de la herramienta de balance? No sé bien cómo gestionarlo en el mío

replies.author: Ecstatic-Bend-104
replies.body: Sure! I have it set up to run batches of simulations where each character/subclass is given two random allies and runs an expedition (via code only, nothing rendered). It tallies the scores of damage, healing, blocked, win/loss, etc into a weighted synergy score, and after a decent sample size I export all of the individual/synergy data to a .csv and have codex provide insights on the scores and make balancing changes or rework specific characters accordingly.
